title: w3id writer vocabulary: upgrade readers before writers
symptom: Readers matching only historical vocabulary terms can miss new firings or transitions. Instance and signature identities must remain unchanged.

detection.description: For a known firing and event ID, collect one native identity binding and populated controls in every explicit dataset. Read both historical and canonical predicates. Missing scope, duplicate bindings, denied/partial/stale reads or unknown installed versions are UNKNOWN.

prerequisites: Exact affected releases and installed writer/reader/shapes digests are still unknown; this draft cannot ship.
Quiesce only the admitted writer; preserve outbox, signing identity, original instance base and receipts.
Capture a pre-upgrade backup and prove a functional restore before changing the store.

steps: Install alias-capable readers and required shapes through the managed lane first.
Prove old and canonical fixtures each resolve one identity; duplicates, unknown terms and incomplete reads refuse.
Deploy the exact new writer artifact while retaining configured instance bases and signing identities.
Verify one admitted native canary and old-record recall; then resume the original schedule and observe its natural run.

validation: Known input event identity matches one native binding.
Legacy record recall and canonical writer vocabulary pass together.
Instance IRI and signed transition bytes are unchanged.
Exact affected/target releases, platform artifacts and admitted command packet are bound before readiness.

rollback.before_new_writes: Restore the prior writer and configuration via the managed inverse.
rollback.after_new_writes: Retain dual readers and stop the scoped writer. Fix forward, or use a separately admitted pre-upgrade backup restore; an old-only reader rollback is unsafe.
rollback.data_loss_limit: Backup restore can lose post-backup writes and requires a separate data-loss admission. No re-key, replay of uncertain effects or signature rewrite.
